questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/2f9e6eff196e24ddabca8d778d27e499fc1b856ef7169257a31a7cbaca8b564b.png)

Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{QP}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{TP}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{TS}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{RS}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{QT}$ in terms of $a,b,c,$ and $d.$
questions.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $Q$ to $T$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{QT}=\overset{\to }{QP}+\overset{\to }{PT},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/e1d5eb2f392332f69fa1507899b30b838a42ebd1c40dacddeca4edcf0f7aa8c2.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{QP}=a,\,\overset{\to }{PT}=-b.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/0e8e24968141284550fac7d4e5c63333789f30ade8f7d5dd8b87fae4e012673a.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{QT} & =\overset{\to }{QP}+\overset{\to }{PT} \\  & =a+(-b) \\  & =a-b\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/86aac25c634d29639329ae53209141ce81a3a82a70d42a4c2dfc6d356ee378b8.png)

In figure $ABCD$ shown above, which of the following are equal to the vector $\overset{\to }{DB}?$

- $\overset{\to }{DA}+\overset{\to }{AC}+\overset{\to }{CB}$
- $\overset{\to }{DA}+\overset{\to }{AB}$
- $\overset{\to }{BA}-\overset{\to }{CA}+\overset{\to }{CD}$
questions.worked_solution:
- For the $1$st expression, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DA}+\overset{\to }{AC}+\overset{\to }{CB} & =(\overset{\to }{DA}+\overset{\to }{AC})+\overset{\to }{CB} \\  & =\overset{\to }{DC}+\overset{\to }{CB} \\  & =\overset{\to }{DB}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- For the $2$nd expression, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DA}+\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{DB}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- For the $3$rd expression, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{BA}-\overset{\to }{CA}+\overset{\to }{CD} & =(\overset{\to }{BA}-\overset{\to }{CA})+\overset{\to }{CD} \\  & =(\overset{\to }{BA}+\overset{\to }{AC})+\overset{\to }{CD} \\  & =\overset{\to }{BC}+\overset{\to }{CD} \\  & =\overset{\to }{BD} \\  & \ne \overset{\to }{DB}\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".

In figure $ABCDEF$ shown above, which of the following are equal to the vector $\overset{\to }{DF}?$

- $\overset{\to }{DC}+\overset{\to }{CB}+\overset{\to }{BF}$
- $\overset{\to }{FB}-\overset{\to }{DB}$
- $\overset{\to }{DE}+\overset{\to }{EF}$
questions.worked_solution:
- For the $1$st expression, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DC}+\overset{\to }{CB}+\overset{\to }{BF} & =(\overset{\to }{DC}+\overset{\to }{CB})+\overset{\to }{BF} \\  & =\overset{\to }{DB}+\overset{\to }{BF} \\  & =\overset{\to }{DF}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- For the $2$nd expression, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{FB}-\overset{\to }{DB} & =\overset{\to }{FB}+\overset{\to }{BD} \\  & =\overset{\to }{FD} \\  & \ne \overset{\to }{DF}\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- For the $3$rd expression, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE}+\overset{\to }{EF} & =\overset{\to }{DF}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".

In figure $ABCDEF$ shown above, which of the following equalities are true?

- $\overset{\to }{BC}-\overset{\to }{DC}=\overset{\to }{BD}$
- $\overset{\to }{BA}+\overset{\to }{AE}-\overset{\to }{FE}=\overset{\to }{BF}$
- $\overset{\to }{CD}-\overset{\to }{ED}-\overset{\to }{FE}=\overset{\to }{FC}$
questions.worked_solution:
- Equality I is true. Indeed, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{BC}-\overset{\to }{DC} & =\overset{\to }{BC}+\overset{\to }{CD} \\  & =\overset{\to }{BD}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Equality II is true. Indeed, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{BA}+\overset{\to }{AE}-\overset{\to }{FE} & =\overset{\to }{BA}+(\overset{\to }{AE}+\overset{\to }{EF}) \\  & =\overset{\to }{BA}+\overset{\to }{AF} \\  & =\overset{\to }{BF}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Equality III is false. Indeed,

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{CD}-\overset{\to }{ED}-\overset{\to }{FE} & =(\overset{\to }{CD}+\overset{\to }{DE})+\overset{\to }{EF} \\  & =\overset{\to }{CE}+\overset{\to }{EF} \\  & =\overset{\to }{CF} \\  & \ne \overset{\to }{FC}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".

$$

- Equality II is true. Indeed, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE}+\overset{\to }{EA}-\overset{\to }{BA} & =\overset{\to }{DE}+(\overset{\to }{EA}+\overset{\to }{AB}) \\  & =\overset{\to }{DE}+\overset{\to }{EB} \\  & =\overset{\to }{DB}.\end{aligned}

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
{\color{blue}\overrightarrow{TS}} = \mathbf{d}, \qquad {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{SQ}}} = -\mathbf{b}.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/08086f7e09568f908aa4919a1156d52e465216221be8908e72a1fd90ec8843dd.png)

  

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TQ} & =\overset{\to }{TS}+\overset{\to }{SQ} \\  & =d+(-b) \\  & =d-b.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Expressing a Vector as a Sum or Difference of More Than Two Known Vectors
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the diagram shown below, where $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\mathbf{a},$ $\overrightarrow{PT}=\mathbf{b},$ and $\overrightarrow{QS}=\mathbf{c}.$ Find $\overrightarrow{TS}$ in terms of $\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},$ and $\mathbf{c}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/04ce04bf7c7f88d6578c74db0d7398a6d299d11bd9f60f4fc4b6e1bfb0129f3b.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $T$ to $S$ consisting only of the vectors $\mathbf a, \mathbf b,$ or $\mathbf c.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
{\color{red}{\overrightarrow{TS}}} = {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{TP}}} + {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{PQ}}} + {\color{blue}{\overrightarrow{QS}}}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/53940607b5cbf0220008e6e31ec60f2fd7fd2e4f70c5a8e95e7fcfd64064b095.png)

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
{\color{blue}\overrightarrow{TP}} = -\mathbf{b}, \qquad {\color{blue}\overrightarrow{PQ}} = \mathbf{a}, \qquad {\color{blue}\overrightarrow{QS}} = \mathbf{c}.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/810cce10eb330b1767a101d9107a9534c437daa123f13056a486a9fc96dbab89.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TS} & =\overset{\to }{TP}+\overset{\to }{PQ}+\overset{\to }{QS} \\  & =-b+a+c \\  & =a-b+c.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/2420154d44b786c6aad54212760e9a37ce67dbdce94a7043039f0e824c5ef9bc.png)

In parallelogram $ABCD$ shown above, which of the following equalities are true?

- $\overrightarrow{CB}+\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{CA}$

- $\overrightarrow{CB}-\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{AC}$

- $\overrightarrow{DC}=\overrightarrow{BA}$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
- Equality I is true. Indeed, $\overrightarrow{CB}+\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{CA}.$

- Equality II is false. Indeed, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{CB}-\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{CB}+\overset{\to }{BA} \\  & =\overset{\to }{CA} \\  & \ne \overset{\to }{AC}\end{aligned}
$$

since $\overrightarrow{CA}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ have opposite directions.

- Equality III is false. Indeed, $\overrightarrow{DC}\neq\overrightarrow{BA}$ since they have opposite directions.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
